---
title: "I keep searching but cannot build an argument"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

## Identify the search problem

What do you need from the next paper? You might need search terms, a missing study or help comparing results. If you already have the evidence but can't explain what it means, try writing before searching again.

## Try this now

1. Write the question your search needs to answer and choose the matching search-ladder level.
2. Record the concepts, sources, dates and signs that you have enough for this purpose.
3. Screen papers for relevance before taking detailed notes.
4. Compare relevant studies in an evidence matrix.
5. Draft what the evidence supports, why it supports it, where studies disagree and what remains uncertain.

## What to take when asking

Show your question, search terms and databases, screening rules and results. Explain which claim you still can't support and how you planned to decide when to stop searching.

## Stop or change route

If similar searches keep returning the same useful material, move to reading and writing. Ask a librarian when translating terms between databases, indexing or coverage is the difficulty.

## You are moving again when

Your next search has a specific purpose. If it doesn't, start comparing the papers you've collected. Keep enough of the search record to repeat it.

Use the [search ladder](../checklists/search-ladder.qmd) and [synthesis map](../templates/synthesis-argument-map.qmd).
